note: One-to-one classification for all 162 proposals; no source repo build/execution claimed.

cases.title: Empty mandatory file
cases.setup: Invoke the existing importer with zero bytes for a required demand file, then with header-only CSV; keep the rest of the fixture valid
cases.expected: Input validation reports empty demand versus missing required schema according to the accepted importer contract; zero shipments and zero committed claims; no crash
cases.v11Reason: Empty/header-only parsing belongs to M1/M4; verify no M5 handoff is issued

cases.title: UTF-8 BOM and line endings
cases.setup: Same two-row synthetic CSV with BOM and without, LF, CRLF, and no trailing newline
cases.expected: Every supported encoding variant yields identical normalized source identities, quantities and planning input; unsupported encoding fails explicitly
cases.v11Reason: BOM and LF/CRLF interpretation belong to importer; normalized M5 records are already the entry point

cases.title: Quoted delimiters
cases.setup: Product display name is quoted CSV field containing comma, escaped quote and an embedded newline; IDs and numeric columns unchanged
cases.expected: Correct parsed fields and unchanged quantity; no shifted destination, group, date or unit columns
cases.v11Reason: CSV quoting/embedded newlines belong to importer; no M5 delimiter parser is in scope

cases.title: Missing or renamed required column
cases.setup: Omit AVAIL_DATE or rename priority field; then reorder all valid columns without changing names
cases.expected: Omission is rejected with column name; reordering yields identical records; do not silently use a neighboring numeric column
cases.v11Reason: Missing/reordered input columns are validated before M5 receives typed records

cases.title: Extra unknown column
cases.setup: Add a harmless Notes column, then an unknown column that collides case-insensitively with a known field
cases.expected: Either documented ignored-column behavior or explicit schema rejection, but never positional misalignment; ambiguous collision rejected
cases.v11Reason: Unknown CSV columns are an importer schema-policy issue

cases.title: Decimal locale and thousands strings
cases.setup: For required integer units test 1200, 1,200, 1.200, 1e3, spaces, and 2.5 under comma-decimal and C locale
cases.expected: Only explicitly supported formats parse, all others fail with field identity; no 1,200 becoming 1 or 2.5 becoming 2
cases.v11Reason: Decimal/thousands separator lexing belongs to importer; M5 never reparses source text

cases.title: Integer overflow before normalization
cases.setup: Set CS=9223372036854775807 and Cases_Unit_Load=1, then multiply by a copy count that overflows 64-bit
cases.expected: Clear range failure before pattern construction; no negative, zero or wrapped allocation; no committed goods
cases.v11Reason: Typed handoff count overflow is already exercised; lexical CSV overflow stays importer hardening

cases.title: NaN and infinity in physical fields
cases.setup: Try case-insensitive nan, +Inf, -Infinity and exponent 1e309 in weight and length fields
cases.expected: Reject every nonfinite or out-of-range value, with source line; do not create proof or fullness flags
cases.v11Reason: NaN/infinite normalized physical values are rejected by current M5 handoff tests

cases.title: Duplicate source key
cases.setup: Two identical source IDs with identical rows; then same ID but different available dates and quantities
cases.expected: Do not ship either duplicate twice; conflict does not silently override one record; identity preserved in report
cases.v11Reason: Duplicate source key with same/conflicting data is already tested

cases.title: Leading-zero identifiers
cases.setup: Resolved master explicitly contains two IDs 001234 and 1234, then compare source labels with leading and trailing spaces
cases.expected: Maintain two distinct resolved products, and use only established M4 normalization; no cross-source merger
cases.v11Reason: M4-resolved leading-zero IDs are kept distinct by M5

cases.title: Mixed metric unit inputs
cases.setup: Synthetic product rows mix inches/cm/mm and lb/kg with exact conversion examples 25.4 mm=1 in and 0.45359237 kg=1 lb
cases.expected: Follow the existing declared unit policy and resolve to identical physical dimensions; unknown unit rejected rather than treated as inches
cases.v11Reason: Existing units-to-loads normalization handoff case; mixed text units themselves are importer concern

cases.title: Invalid and leap dates
cases.expected: Invalid calendar dates rejected; 2028-02-29 accepted; required ordering and ten-day windows use exact day differences
cases.v11Reason: Bad calendar string parsing and leap-day date lexing belong to importer

cases.title: Time-of-day and time-zone fields
cases.setup: Provide dates as midnight UTC versus local-offset timestamps that fall on the previous calendar date
cases.expected: Apply only the documented date schema and timezone interpretation; unsupported timestamps rejected, never shifted silently across eligibility boundary
cases.v11Reason: Time zones and time-of-day parsing belong to importer; M5 consumes normalized ship-day values

cases.title: Very long field and Unicode source
cases.setup: Use a 100000-character quoted description and non-ASCII display name; actual identifier is fixed ASCII
cases.expected: No truncated identifier or buffer overrun; report's ASCII policy is applied to output without changing the internal source identity
cases.v11Reason: Extreme Unicode/length handling of input fields belongs to importer; report escape covered elsewhere

cases.title: Reservation rows with same lane-date
cases.setup: Two identical reservation rows, then two valid distinct records, then a conflicting equipment type for same lane-date
cases.expected: Documented skip or aggregation policy is explicit; no hidden double reservation; differing equipment is never guessed or silently merged
cases.v11Reason: Duplicate reservation records do not create duplicate available slots

cases.title: File paths with spaces and nonroot working directory
cases.setup: Run the same tiny fixture from repo root and a sibling folder using absolute and relative input paths that include spaces
cases.expected: Identical normalized result or an explicit path error; no accidental use of test-fixture fallback
cases.v11Reason: File path portability belongs to CLI/importer; M5 direct seam sees typed values

cases.title: Exact width equality
cases.setup: One rigid nonrotatable 100 x 20 x 108 in footprint in 100-inch-wide trailer
cases.expected: Fits exactly across width, provided other limits allow; layout witness inside walls with no tolerance inflation
cases.v11Reason: The exact width/length boundary is explicitly tested

cases.title: Three-across epsilon boundary
cases.setup: Three equal rigid widths 33.3333333 versus 33.3333334 inches, with zero allowed spacing and suitable length
cases.expected: Three-wide row fits first case (99.9999999), fails second (100.0000002); never decide on rounded 33.3 display
cases.v11Reason: Three-across candidate generator uses <=33.3, not 100/3; distinguish row pattern from physical certificate
cases.v12Fixture: Row-generator control: one row of three unrotated rigid 33.30 x 20 in footprints (all 80 in high, 100 lb, fixed) in width 100. Repeat with short sides one supported input step above 33.30 in (33.31 in at 0.01-in normalization, or the repository's documented normalized precision). All other limits unbound and no other atoms.
cases.v12Expected: At 33.30 in, a three-across candidate is generated (3*33.30 = 99.90 <= 100). At one supported input step above 33.30 in (33.31 in by default), the literal M4 test side <= 33.3 excludes that three-across candidate. With the 0.01-in step the summed width is still 99.93 <= 100, so absence of the pattern is NOT a proof that no rectangular layout can exist. If normalized precision differs, recompute the geometric sum and keep candidate-generation status separate from a physical infeasibility proof. A supplied-witness check remains independent.
cases.v12Oracle: DIRECT row-candidate enumeration + exact decimal width arithmetic and isolated witness validation.

cases.title: Two-across exact boundary
cases.setup: Two 50-inch-wide stacks versus one 50 and one 50.000001, with geometry otherwise identical
cases.expected: The first pair fits a 100-inch width; second does not in that orientation; any alternate feasible layout must have its own valid witness
cases.v11Reason: Verify two 50-in widths exactly fit and +delta is rejected by the same orientation
cases.v12Fixture: A direct row check in a width-100 trailer, two nonstackable rigid rectangles with across widths exactly 50.00 and 50.00 in; then increase the first width by one supported input step (50.01 in at 0.01-in normalization, or the repository's documented normalized precision). Hold orientation fixed. Height 80 in, weight 100 lb each.
cases.v12Expected: The first declared orientation sums to exactly 100.00 in and fits; increasing the first width by one supported input step makes that row wider than 100 (100.01 in for a 0.01-in step), so the declared row fails. Do not claim the complete floor cannot fit after a different legal orientation.
cases.v12Oracle: Exact rational row-width check and independent orientation search.

cases.title: Rotation-only placement
cases.setup: Two rigid rectangles 100x20 and 20x100 in a 100-inch width with explicit allowed floor rotation
cases.expected: A valid arrangement may use a legal orientation for each; forbidden orientation cases do not rotate; witness records orientation
cases.v11Reason: Make the legal rotation the sole way a specific rigid atom can fit
cases.v12Fixture: Rigid atom floor footprint 80 x 55 in, in a 60 x 100 in trailer floor, height 80 in, weight 100 lb. Floor rotation is allowed.
cases.v12Expected: Original 80-length orientation cannot fit length 60; turned footprint 55-length x 80-width does fit. A solver that never considers allowed rotation fails.
cases.v12Oracle: Enumerate both exact rectangle orientations, check one witness.

cases.title: Exact trailer height including deck
cases.setup: Two stack variants have 102-inch content plus 6-inch deck and 102.000001-inch content plus 6-inch deck
cases.expected: First is exactly 108 inches and allowed, second exceeds and is rejected; no deck added twice
cases.v11Reason: Deck-inclusive height equality and just-over are specified

cases.title: Stackability blocked by display
cases.setup: Two 50-inch-high units with 6-inch deck each physically could form 112 inches; also a nonstackable display at height 40
cases.expected: Deck/height and nonstackability prohibit illegal joining regardless of tempting floor savings
cases.v11Reason: Non-stackable display cannot gain illegal height or floor positions

cases.title: Rounded 48 versus 48.01 inches
cases.setup: Use width 48 and 48.01 in a 96.005-inch-wide synthetic trailer with no tolerance; compare 48+48 and 48.01+48.01
cases.expected: 48+48 fits, 48.01+48.01 does not; identical report-rounded widths cannot alter legality
cases.v11Reason: Full-precision near-equal dimensions/weight control is present

cases.title: Row grouping false impossibility
cases.setup: Use exact Tom R-5a layout and nine distractor variants from the known fixture package
cases.expected: Oracle finds 23 unit loads in all variants; heuristic refusal or stopped grouping never produces a proven no-fit or optimality claim
cases.v11Reason: Exact Tom row-grouping regression with witness/proof restrictions is present

cases.title: Overlapping rectangle witness
cases.setup: Provide layout of two same-height 60x60 rectangles with origins (0,0) and (50,0)
cases.expected: Independent witness validator rejects 10-inch overlap, even if reported cube and total length are legal
cases.v11Reason: Overlap invalidates a supplied layout witness

cases.title: Out-of-bounds witness after translation
cases.setup: Truck length 630; supplied 20x100 rectangle with x origin 611
cases.expected: Reject because extent 631 exceeds trailer; positive origin and apparently valid row count do not excuse it
cases.v11Reason: Translation beyond trailer end is an existing invalid-witness variant

cases.title: Supplied witness with exhausted search
cases.setup: Inject zero grouping-search permits but provide a legal complete layout witness for final candidate
cases.expected: Verification of supplied witness succeeds; no search-backed optimality claim; failure to search does not invalidate already checked feasibility
cases.v11Reason: Checked supplied witness remains valid despite exhausted search budget

cases.title: Cache footprint version change
cases.setup: Copy a cached 20x100 pattern, then change that product's width to 20.1 under a different product-master version
cases.expected: Re-evaluate geometry; cached approval cannot be reused without the effective dimension identity; no source quantity lost
cases.v11Reason: Product-master change invalidates stale weight and cached packing

cases.title: Permitted pinwheel switch
cases.setup: Use a small independently enumerated footprint set with at least one legal pinwheel layout and a control where pinwheel is disabled
cases.expected: Legal witness is found when enabled; disabled control cannot claim that same orientation as an allowed pattern
cases.v11Reason: Pinwheel and supported orientation generation are explicitly in the case

cases.title: Incomplete search cannot prove no-fit
cases.setup: Search same geometrically feasible fixture under 0, 1 and sufficient state budgets
cases.expected: Insufficient budget returns Undecided unless independent impossibility certificate exists; sufficient budget returns Fits with complete witness
cases.v11Reason: Interrupted no-fit is Unknown, never a certificate of impossibility

cases.title: Exact weight boundary
cases.setup: Use 2 indivisible loads of 22500 lb on trailer payload 45000 and a third load of 0.001 lb
cases.expected: First pair legal at equality; the third cannot be added; no epsilon permits overweight
cases.v11Reason: Ensure 45000.000000 fits and one supported positive increment fails, independent of fullness labels
cases.v12Fixture: One nonstackable item of 20 x 100 x 90 in, mass exactly 45000.00 lb in a 630 x 100 x 108 in/45000-lb truck; repeat at one supported input step above the payload limit (45000.01 lb at 0.01-lb normalization, or the repository's documented normalized precision). No other cargo.
cases.v12Expected: At payload equality the truck is legal; at one supported input step above the limit it is illegal. FULL labels have no authority to relax the physical limit. Use full normalized input precision at the typed physical seam (0.01 lb unless the repository documents another step).
cases.v12Oracle: Full-precision independent mass comparison.

cases.title: One indivisible overweight atom
cases.setup: One prebuilt 45000.01-lb stack, one free truck with 45000-lb limit
cases.expected: No dispatch; item identified as physically unshippable rather than claimed eligible overflow
cases.v11Reason: An indivisible unit heavier than the truck is rejected

cases.title: Component unit-load cap versus atoms
cases.setup: Two rigid identical-geometry stacks containing 2 and 3 unit loads, 5-unit cap, one reserved truck
cases.expected: Both can fit if geometry/weight permit; count 5, not 2 stacks; adding a third 1-unit atom exceeds cap
cases.v11Reason: Component unit-load coefficients, not atom count, govern cap selection

cases.title: Cap 7 to 5 to 7 in same process
cases.setup: Two loads per atom, 4 legal atoms, same trailer and product IDs, with cap profiles 7, 5 and 7
cases.expected: Maximum number of atoms by cap is 3, 2 and 3 respectively; old physical approval and proof data not reused
cases.v11Reason: Cap 7/5/7 cache and proof invalidation already specified

cases.title: Invalid unit-load-cap config
cases.setup: Try absent, 0, -1, 1, 64, 65, 1.5, NaN and 9223372036854775808 in a required field
cases.expected: Invalid values rejected; cap 1,64,65 accepted subject to declared limits; never silently fall back to 64
cases.v11Reason: Missing/zero/fractional/overflowing cap rejected at input seam

cases.title: One atom exceeds cap
cases.setup: One rigid 3-unit-load stack against a 2-unit-load trailer cap
cases.expected: Do not split the rigid stack to evade cap; report undeliverable under that equipment with source quantities intact
cases.v11Reason: Atom with 6 indivisible unit loads against cap 5 is never split or loaded
cases.v12Fixture: One indivisible prebuilt atom 48 x 36 x 90 in, weight 600 lb, 6 source unit loads; one slot with cap 5 and ample other limits. Control cap 6.
cases.v12Expected: At cap 5 the entire atom is left, no 5-of-6 split; at cap 6 the atom may ship intact. Count and source conservation are exact.
cases.v12Oracle: Integer whole-atom subset enumerator and per-source ledger.

cases.title: Two constraints bind together
cases.setup: One full candidate is 45000 lb and contains exactly 64 unit loads, with a valid complete floor witness
cases.expected: May dispatch at equality; adding any positive-weight or 1-unit-load atom violates at least one hard constraint
cases.v11Reason: Two hard limits exactly bind; next atom violates both and cannot be admitted
cases.v12Fixture: A rigid nonstackable atom 630 x 100 x 80 in, gross 45000 lb, one source unit load. Trailer floor 630 x 100, height 108, payload 45000. Attempt adding a second 1 x 1 x 80 in, 1 lb atom.
cases.v12Expected: First atom exactly binds floor coverage and payload. It fits alone; no supported disjoint floor position or payload remains for the second. Candidate claiming to ship both is rejected independently of cube/fullness.
cases.v12Oracle: Rectangle non-overlap/inside-trailer witness checker and exact payload arithmetic.

cases.title: Different trailer type for entire run
cases.setup: Run same physical fixture with 630x100x108/45000 and 480x92x108/30000 configured trailers
cases.expected: Each result uses actual configured geometry/weight/cap; no implicit 53F fallback; reject unknown type
cases.v11Reason: Different single run trailer type uses exact container dimensions

cases.title: Unsupported mixed equipment in one lane-date
cases.setup: Input calls for one reservation of type A and one of type B on same lane-date under current feed capability
cases.expected: Explicit unsupported-input status without guess, fabricated homogeneous slots or committed sources; future support is separate decision
cases.v11Reason: Current input rejects unsupported mixed types with reason; no guessed single default
cases.v12Fixture: At normal run adapter, availability advertises a single lane-date with one slot of equipment A and one slot of equipment B with different dimensions; no supported typed-slot selection feed is supplied.
cases.v12Expected: Return explicit unsupported mixed-equipment status, no guessed 53F homogeneous default and no inventory/reservation commits. Do not prevent direct physical adapter tests with explicit independent slot capabilities.
cases.v12Oracle: Input-to-M5 integration status and unchanged state oracle; current C9 scope.

cases.title: Typed availability matrix future scope
cases.setup: Synthetic availability says 2 A + 5 B + 1 C trucks at same lane-date, each with declared distinct limits
cases.expected: Record expected future semantics only as CONDITIONAL; current limited feed path rejects clearly without losing source or reservation identity
cases.v11Reason: Truck-type inventory matrix and mixed fleet composition require a new input contract accepted as future scope

cases.title: Missing trailer capability fields
cases.setup: Valid equipment name but payload or unit-load cap missing from its actual catalog entry
cases.expected: Reject unsupported capability before planning, rather than inserting 45000 or 64 as silent defaults
cases.v11Reason: Alternate trailer without payload/unit cap is rejected, no defaulting

cases.title: Length equality and one-micron excess
cases.setup: One rigid 630x100 footprint and one 630.000001x100 footprint in a 630-inch trailer
cases.expected: First fits alone at exact equality, second is non-fitting unless an allowed 90-degree turn truly makes it fit
cases.v11Reason: Trailer length exactly at boundary versus one input-supported microunit excess
cases.v12Fixture: A single fixed rectangle floor length exactly 630.00 in, width 100 in, height 80 in, 100 lb in standard trailer. Control 630.01 in; floor rotation would exceed width 100.
cases.v12Expected: Exact length fits, 630.01 does not. No report-rounding or floor-search grain may turn the excess into a legal witness. Use input-supported 0.01-in test precision (not an assumed micron parser).
cases.v12Oracle: Exact normalized length comparisons; supplied-witness validation.

cases.title: Required goods before can-go
cases.setup: One reservation fits one FX-30 full truck; 30 due-D P11 goods and 30 due-D+1 P0 can-go goods all available D
cases.expected: All 30 required goods ship before any can-go under recorded required-first rule; later urgency must not displace required
cases.v11Reason: Required cargo outranks can-go across shared reservations

cases.title: Overdue date beats nominal priority
cases.setup: One truck fits 30 units; 30 overdue P11 versus 30 due-today P0, all available D, AgeFirst
cases.expected: Overdue P11 ships; when effective PriorityFirst is explicitly selected, P0 ships; defer per-lane integration if not in scope
cases.v11Reason: AgeFirst picks older P11 over newer P0 under its explicit fixture

cases.title: Strict original due date after carry
cases.setup: 30 due D-4 remain, then compete against 30 due D P0 on D with AgeFirst
cases.expected: Original D-4 rank stays older after carry and wins; carried-record processing date never replaces original due date
cases.v11Reason: Carried goods preserve original age for urgency comparison

cases.title: 10-day pull boundary and availability
cases.setup: Demand due D+10, D+11, and D+3 with available D+1; pull limit 10, departure D
cases.expected: D+10 eligible, D+11 not, D+3 not available; check at component level inside any stack
cases.v11Reason: Can-go outside pull window is excluded even with availability

cases.title: Mixed component stack prevents future leakage
cases.setup: Two stackable 20x100x50 TLD components due D and D+1, both available D; one grouped stack, pull OFF
cases.expected: Mixed stack is ineligible on D or is decomposed only if M4's documented atom contract permits it; never hide future unit inside due-D stack
cases.v11Reason: Mixed component stack cannot smuggle future-unavailable units

cases.title: Can-go-only existing reservation
cases.setup: M5 direct entry, 21 reserved, zero due-D units and ten eligible due-D+1 units, pull ON
cases.expected: Can-go can use existing legal capacity; no required cargo invented; selected future stock withdrawn once
cases.v11Reason: Existing date with can-go only does not prematurely exit

cases.title: Impossible required cannot block feasible service forever
cases.setup: One 630.01x100 unrotatable required atom and 30 FX-30 eligible can-go atoms with one available truck
cases.expected: Impossible required identified separately and never shipped; feasible can-go can ship if approved priority/fallback contract allows, without misreporting all-required success
cases.v11Reason: Impossible required atom cannot deadlock eligible feasible future goods

cases.title: Carry and pull same source offered twice
cases.setup: Demand source S has 30 units due D+1, both linked dates D and D+1 available to plan from independent snapshots
cases.expected: At most 30 total units ship across both dates; selection on D subtracts exactly those units before D+1, no duplicate source references
cases.v11Reason: Selected future draw is deducted exactly once on later date

cases.title: Two destinations with same product ID
cases.setup: One origin, two destinations each have product 123 and a single reservation on D
cases.expected: No goods cross destination, no reservation appears at the other lane; isolated ledger identities
cases.v11Reason: Same product on different destinations cannot cross reservation identity

cases.title: Zero-day pull window
cases.setup: Pull ON but configured limit zero; one unit due D and one due D+1
cases.expected: Only due-D unit date-eligible; ON0 is not an accidental 10-day fallback
cases.v11Reason: A configured zero-day pull window permits only same-day demand
cases.v12Fixture: One date D and a can-go demand source originally due D+1 (available D), pull-forward ON but maxDaysPulledForward=0. One existing D reservation, no required goods.
cases.v12Expected: Future D+1 demand does not ship on D under zero-day window, remains available for its actual date. A due-D control may ship. No date is invented.
cases.v12Oracle: Exact date arithmetic and source/date ledger.

cases.title: Date arithmetic leap and year boundary
cases.setup: Departure 2028-02-20 plus ten days and 2026-12-25 plus ten days
cases.expected: Results 2028-03-01 and 2027-01-04 respectively; no 86400-second/timezone drift
cases.v11Reason: Leap and year-boundary day arithmetic already tested

cases.title: Unknown priority fails early
cases.setup: Test P-1, P12, P99, blank and string urgent against declared 0..11 priority domain
cases.expected: Each invalid priority rejected or quarantined with exact source; never clamped to P0/P11
cases.v11Reason: Invalid priority outside supported rank domain is rejected

cases.title: Equal-age all same-class tie
cases.setup: Two sources each 30 FX-30 units, same due date, same urgency and group constraints, one truck
cases.expected: Use declared fairness/canonical rule, not unstable row order; both results physically feasible
cases.v11Reason: ED-21 includes equal-class canonical source-line tie

cases.title: Reservation absent while demand exists
cases.setup: One required FX-30 stack, no slots on current date and one slot four days later with carry ON
cases.expected: None ships on unreserved D; eligible carry moves once to actual later reserved date preserving source and due date
cases.v11Reason: Goods with zero reservation do not consume/ship trucks

cases.title: Linked-date selection evaluated in reverse order
cases.setup: Two linked ship dates with eligible pull/carry and one shared source, evaluate construction order forward then reverse
cases.expected: Final chosen linked-date solution obeys temporal inventory accounting and no double shipment, regardless of build ordering
cases.v11Reason: Reverse order of source rows for linked dates; no duplicate goods and exact selected deltas
cases.v12Fixture: Two one-slot lane-dates D and D+1, slot cap 15, same group. Twenty individually traceable unit loads due D+1 and available D; pull forward ON, ten-day window, no other required goods. Compare input records in normal and reversed source/date-row order, using the same chronological planner policy.
cases.v12Expected: Both row permutations produce the same selected original-source allocations and deltas under that deterministic policy. At most 15 ship on either date, at most 20 total, no duplicate carry/pull source claim. Do not change the algorithm to plan dates in reverse chronological order.
cases.v12Oracle: Independent source ledger and chosen plan canonicalization; exact date-window check.

cases.title: Threshold boundary 20 and 21
cases.setup: Identical lane-dates differing only in reserved count 20 versus 21, T=20
cases.expected: 20 stays M4; 21 routes M5; no method chosen from historical client built count
cases.v11Reason: 21 versus configured 20 route boundary has direct control

cases.title: Configurable threshold not hard-coded
cases.setup: Use T=20 and T=50 on same 21-reservation lane-date
cases.expected: With T20 route M5; with T50 do not route M5; retained result profile identifies chosen threshold
cases.v11Reason: Alternate threshold 50 proves routing is configurable

cases.title: M5 absent fallback invariant
cases.setup: Run at 21 reservations with M5 planner unavailable, compare corrected baseline M4 behavior bytewise after normalized volatile fields
cases.expected: No new shipment or silent drop; clearly marked escalation status consistent with accepted M4 fallback
cases.v11Reason: When no M5 planner is installed, the M4 path must remain byte-for-byte unchanged
cases.v12Fixture: A lane with 21 reserved trucks and valid required goods reaches the M4 selector while no M5 LargeLanePlanner has been injected. Compare with the exact known M4 behavior at the accepted commit.
cases.v12Expected: The normal M4 fallback behavior, including its previously reported escalation/no-plan result, source status, and absence of commits, remains unchanged. No recursive M5 invocation and no fabricated successful plan.
cases.v12Oracle: Read-only exact M4 baseline replay and source/result fingerprint.

cases.title: Rolling block 21
cases.setup: 21 reserved with 21 homogeneous one-truck atoms and Method B block size 19
cases.expected: The schedule is 19+2, no padding to 38, sources claimed once
cases.v11Reason: 21 trucks form a full 19-block and short second block

cases.title: Rolling block 38 and 39
cases.setup: 38 and 39 homogeneous whole-truck atoms with 38/39 reserved and block size 19
cases.expected: Schedules 19+19 and 19+19+1; no artificial last-block capacity
cases.v11Reason: Add 39-slot case with 19+19+1 and no invented cargo
cases.v12Fixture: Thirty-nine FX-BLOCK rigid atoms, each exactly fills one reserved trailer; 39 reservations and block size 19, one group/priority/date.
cases.v12Expected: Method B processes accepted nonempty blocks 19 + 19 + 1, never invents a 40th load or pads with a phantom item; all 39 atoms ship once. The final block consumes one valid reservation.
cases.v12Oracle: Count-only class oracle and source/reservation ledger.

cases.title: Same lane-date groups share reservations
cases.setup: Group A 20 whole-truck atoms and B 20 whole-truck atoms, 21 reservations on same date
cases.expected: Total dispatched <=21 and comparator chooses groups globally; never 21 per group
cases.v11Reason: Groups compete across one shared lane-date reservation ceiling

cases.title: Duplicate reservation row idempotence
cases.setup: Same reservation record appears twice, then unique records with equal types
cases.expected: Duplicate does not double count and distinct records remain distinct under declared source identity
cases.v11Reason: Duplicate reservation record and distinct equal-valued records are separate

cases.title: No goods but 21 reserved
cases.setup: One lane-date with 21 slots and no eligible source goods
cases.expected: Zero dispatch, 21 unused slots; NOT an algorithm timeout and not a fabricated empty shipment
cases.v11Reason: A completed empty run is not a timeout, and reservation count remains unchanged

cases.title: Date-scoped reservations
cases.setup: Same lane has 21 slots on D and 20 on D+1; combined benchmark contains historical 38 built trucks
cases.expected: Each date keeps its own slot limit; benchmark may not pool 41 slots or use 38 as a cap
cases.v11Reason: The joined reference keeps independent 21/20 date pools

cases.title: Unknown trailer with availability
cases.setup: Reservation gives blank type, then known 53F, then an unknown type Z99
cases.expected: Only supported case uses verified catalog; blank/unknown handled by declared explicit error, never guessed
cases.v11Reason: Unknown equipment type with availability must fail before planning, never choose 53F
cases.v12Fixture: Single-lane availability row refers to unknown equipment code UNKNOWN_TYPE (not in the capabilities catalogue); sufficient valid demand, 21 reservations. Keep all other fields legal.
cases.v12Expected: Reject the planning input with unknown-equipment reason before any candidate or commit; do not use 53F payload or cap as default.
cases.v12Oracle: Config catalogue lookup and unchanged-state oracle.

cases.title: Reservation count 100 plus
cases.setup: 100 reserved slots, 3 full-truck atoms available, Method B block size 19
cases.expected: Exactly 3 nonempty trucks maximum; 97 unused; no 100 fabricated shipments or 19-slot padding
cases.v11Reason: Count 101 reserves accurately without needing to create empty shipments
cases.v12Fixture: One FX-30 source unit load and 101 equal homogeneous reservations on one date. No fake cargo is provided. Run direct or through supported routing.
cases.v12Expected: Exactly one used/nonempty truck and 100 unused reservations if no other cargo; no fabricated empty loads. Do not infer a numeric penalty when penalty rate is unknown.
cases.v12Oracle: Count and independent source/reservation ledger.

cases.title: Threshold change while plan is in flight
cases.setup: Create immutable plan context with T=20 and change external config to T=25 before commit
cases.expected: Plan stays bound to its recorded context; stale global config cannot silently change route/validation; replan if version mismatch
cases.v11Reason: Changing config after planning starts cannot change frozen routing decision
cases.v12Fixture: Start a 21-reservation lane-date with routing threshold 20, freeze context and enter the M5 planner. While a fake-clock planner is paused, change live configuration threshold to 50; then start a fresh separate lane-date run.
cases.v12Expected: In-flight run stays routed via threshold 20 and validates against its frozen version. Fresh run with threshold 50 follows normal M4 routing. Neither run consumes the other snapshot; no cache contamination.
